requirements.requirement: node2 and node3 can reach each other over forwarded TCP port 8080 through node1
requirements.summary: socat connections to port 8080 succeeded in both directions (node2->node3 and node3->node2), confirmed both before and after every node's restart, returning the expected listener payload each time.

requirements.requirement: node1 refuses forwarded TCP port 23 traffic between node2 and node3
requirements.summary: An nftables forward-chain rule rejects TCP/23 with TCP RST in both directions; connection attempts on port 23 consistently returned 'Connection refused' both before and after every node restart, confirming the reject rule is active and effective, not merely configured.

requirements.requirement: all other forwarded traffic between node2 and node3 is left untouched
requirements.summary: ICMP ping between node2 and node3 through node1 succeeded with 0% loss both before the ACL was applied and after every node restart, demonstrating the default-accept forward policy remains in effect for traffic other than TCP/23.

requirements.requirement: Provider-wide node-restart evidence protocol executed on all managed nodes (independent check)
requirements.summary: For all three nodes, a pre-restart healthy baseline (boot_id, addressing, ACL/rules, forwarding sysctls) was captured, a restart was acknowledged, a distinct post-restart boot_id was observed (node1: 1eda2df4->2a3a2bed, node2: 5b620f5a->133a57a5, node3: 2c237d4f->cb0a4926, matching the fixed after-prepare/after-executor boot-identity snapshots), and full functional recovery (addressing, routing, ACL behavior, forwarding sysctls, service state) was verified afterward on each node.

overall_summary: All three material outcomes of the task are directly and consistently satisfied: node2 and node3 can reach each other on forwarded TCP/8080 through node1, node1 actively rejects forwarded TCP/23 with a TCP RST (not just configured but behaviorally confirmed), and other forwarded traffic (ICMP) is left untouched. This behavior was verified both before and after a full sequential restart of all three nodes, with clear pre-restart baselines, changed boot identities, and post-restart functional recovery for each node, satisfying the independent restart-evidence protocol as well. The only shortcoming is leftover test infrastructure (open firewalld ports for 23/8080 and a running socat listener on port 23 on node3, plus stray log files) that was not cleaned up after verification, which is a minor hygiene issue rather than a functional gap.
limitations: Only ICMP was exercised as a representative example of 'other forwarded traffic'; no other protocols (e.g., UDP, other TCP ports) were tested to confirm they remain unaffected, though the nftables default-accept policy design and the reject rule's port-23-specific scope make this a low-risk gap.

Test artifacts (socat listeners on 8080/23 and associated firewalld port openings, plus log files) were left in place on node2/node3 at the end of the session; these do not affect the enforced ACL on node1 but represent minor uncleaned residue.
The nftables reject rule for TCP/23 was validated using a socat test client/listener rather than a real telnet client, but this is functionally equivalent for a TCP-based protocol rejection test.

operational_hygiene.summary: The material task changes (static addressing on node1/node2/node3, forwarding sysctls, the nftables transit_acl table, and the transit-acl.service) were all necessary, persisted appropriately, and none were destructive or unnecessary. One failed discovery command (cmd-8b4dcd03eb01438c, 'config interface ip add eth1...') was a no-op on SONiC and caused no state change. However, the executor left test/diagnostic residue in place at task completion: firewalld runtime rules opening TCP 23 and 8080 were added on node2 and node3 (cmd-3a5b1a8c058f45a3, cmd-e21052e19a3c4269) and re-applied after each reboot (cmd-7d6eb25cca854fbd, cmd-4c33a0b9065846b2) to support functional testing, and socat test listeners on ports 8080/23 plus their /tmp log files were started on node3 (cmd-1456f99e78b349e8, cmd-4c33a0b9065846b2) and left running in the final after-executor snapshot (node3 shows 0.0.0.0:23 and 0.0.0.0:8080 socat listeners still active, and /tmp/l23.log, /tmp/l8080.log, /tmp/reboot.log remain on node2 and node3). These are bounded, low-risk, and directly tied to verifying the task's functional requirement, but they were not cleaned up afterward, leaving an open TCP/23 listener and firewall exposure on node3 unrelated to the persisted task configuration.
